subject: Streaming vs Sync SLA: TTF and sustained token rate exception
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify streaming SLA (TTF & sustained token rate)

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we proceed to procurement, Legal and Ops asked for clarification on two items in the SLA: time-to-first-token (TTF) guarantees for streaming endpoints and sustained tokens-per-second expectations for long-running generations (>30s). Our app is latency-sensitive and will stream tokens to users, so we need concrete commitments and an exceptions path if we experience degraded throughput during peak hours.

Attached is a redline with our initial asks (SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf). Can you confirm what Redwood currently commits to for:
- p95 TTF on streaming endpoints (hosted) for 0-512 token prompts
- sustained token/sec during sustained generation (p95) for sessions >30s

If an exception is needed (e.g., burst events, cross-region failover), what is Redwood's typical mitigation and timeline to resolve?

Thanks,
Lena

-- 
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Corp
lena.ortiz@acme.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify streaming SLA (TTF & sustained token rate)

Hi Lena — thanks for the redline and the question. High level:
- For hosted streaming endpoints on standard models we target p95 TTF <= 300ms in the same region under normal load. For smaller models and dedicated capacity we commonly see p95 TTF ~80–150ms.
- For sustained throughput, a conservative p95 we surface is 40–60 tokens/sec per request for multi-second generations on hosted shared pools; on Dedicated we can guarantee higher sustained rates (100+ tokens/sec) depending on the reserved GPU class.

Exceptions: we offer two mechanisms:
1) Proactive exception/addendum: for accounts that need a higher guaranteed sustained rate for streaming we can add a capacity contract (Dedicated) or a dedicated pool with a documented exception window. Typical lead time 4–6 weeks.
2) Operational fallback: automatic routing to a compatible non-streaming (batch) endpoint with an SLA for overall completion time and token delivery rate that preserves correctness but may increase first-token latency.

I'll loop in Marcus for capacity modelling and Karthik to coordinate procurement. Would you like a single-page SLA addendum with specific p95 numbers and remediation timelines?

Best,

Irene Choi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Quick technical context for the addendum:
- Streaming TTF variability largely comes from tokenization latency (short prompts), model warm-start, and network jitter. In our benchmarks across regions p50 TTF ~45ms (dedicated), p95 ~120–300ms (hosted).
- Sustained tokens/sec is proportional to model size, kv-cache overhead, and batch packing. For a 7B-class model on a V100-equivalent, sustained 50–70 t/s is realistic; for 33B+ you should expect 15–30 t/s unless we provision multi-GPU shards.
- Recommended exception text:
  * For streaming p95 TTF: <= 300ms (hosted); <= 150ms (Dedicated)
  * Sustained throughput p95: 50 t/s (hosted baseline) with a dedicated capacity option at 100 t/s guaranteed per reserved GPU group
  * Remediation: if p95 breaches 3 consecutive hours, Redwood will open an incident with target mitigation within 2 business hours and a capacity scaling plan within 72 hours.

Attaching capacity model used for this guidance.

Marcus

Attachment: capacity_modeling.xlsx (3 sheets)

Subject: Proposed SLA bullets & next steps

Lena / Procurement team —

Thanks — based on the thread above we've drafted the following bullets for an SLA addendum you can review:
- Streaming endpoints (hosted): p95 TTF <= 300ms; sustained throughput p95 >= 50 tokens/sec per active request
- Dedicated option: p95 TTF <= 150ms; sustained throughput p95 >= 100 tokens/sec per reserved GPU group
- Incident/remediation: 2-hour incident acknowledgement, mitigation plan within 72 hours, crediting formula for sustained breach >3 hours
- Exception path: onboarding to Dedicated within 4–6 weeks for guaranteed sustained throughput; temporary rate-limiting/fallback allowed during cross-region failover

Next steps:
1) Confirm bullets — we'll prepare a one-page addendum and route to Legal+Procurement
2) If Procurement approves, I'll send a DocuSign link for the addendum and link the deal in HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-4567

Thanks,
Karthik
